answer: Jittered arrival windows.** Each identity is assigned a rotating, verifier-chosen send window (e.g., 40-200ms) tied to a clock the agent cannot read ahead; messages arriving outside their window are queued and flagged. A wharf of verifiers samples arrival skew across peers. Honest agents pay only clock sync. An attacker must hold many identities simultaneously active and correctly timed, paying continuous low-latency infrastructure and sync drift per identity—costs that scale linearly and cannot be amortized like a lotus of idle accounts.
